title: Penguin Bowling
tagline: Belly-slide a chubby penguin down the ice and knock over snowmen and fish!
howToPlay: Swipe up (or pull back and let go) to slide the penguin down the ice. A curvy swipe makes it curve! On a keyboard, ← → aim and Space slides; ◀ ▶ move the penguin. Bumpers 🛟 keep the penguin out of the gutters. Each fresh rack starts with a plan: the youngest pick 'a few' or 'a lot' from two pictures, and stand near the edge or in the middle to make it happen. After every roll, tap each pin still standing to count it (fallen ones don't count), then say how many: the last number counted tells how many, and fallen and standing always make 10. Children who count carefully work out the missing part instead while a snow cloud hides the pins (7 + ? = 10, or ? + 2 = 10), first from three numbers, later from a 1–10 strip. Their plans use numbers: 'knock down 8' (for the first two plans of a game, footprints and a number show where to stand; then the child finds the spot: the middle knocks many, the edge just one), and later 'leave 2 standing', which takes the bond to turn into where to stand, or a curved plan like 'leave 7 ↪' that sets the curve. A plan that comes out just right asks for the other part. Before a second roll, say where the pins are or which side has more: footprints show where to walk, fewer as the child grows, until the spare is their own plan. Tap 💭 to guess how many will fall first. Pick Ages 3–5 to start with counting, or 6–8 to start with missing parts; either way the game adapts as the child plays. Games are 5 frames; pick 10 for a longer one.
learning: Number bonds to 10, counting, predictions and spatial reasoning
